issues.detail: The Greek 'σπιλαδες' (spilades) means 'spots' or 'stains', not 'vết nhơ' in the sense of a 'bữa tiệc' (feast/party). The Vietnamese translation adds 'bữa tiệc' (feast) which is not present in the Greek text. The Greek describes them as 'spots' within your loves.

The Greek 'συνευωχουμενοι' (syneuchomomenoi) means 'rejoicing together'. The Vietnamese 'dự tiệc cùng nhau' (attending a feast together) changes the nature of the action from 'rejoicing' to 'attending a party'.
